A.name: Southside Youth Peace Collective (synthetic sample)
A.profile: Grassroots, founded 2023, 4 staff (2 full time), about $310K budget. A neighborhood-rooted violence interruption and youth mentoring group in its third year. Credibility with young people and families is its greatest asset; nearly all back-office function runs through the founder and executive director. Funding is one city contract plus small individual gifts.

B.name: Riverbend Violence Interruption Network (synthetic sample)
B.profile: Mid-size, founded 2016, 19 staff, about $2.1M budget. An established CVI provider operating hospital-based intervention and street outreach across two precincts. Core systems exist and are used, but they are uneven: the board is functioning yet thin on finance expertise, and evaluation is still mostly output counting. Roughly 80% of revenue is restricted government funding.

C.name: Metro Community Safety Alliance (synthetic sample)
C.profile: Mature, founded 2009, 48 staff, about $7.4M budget. A regional anchor organization running CVI programming, a training institute for peer organizations, and a policy shop. Most domains are mature and integrated. The remaining work is at the top of the ladder: an endowment-grade reserve strategy, independent impact evaluation, and modernizing data infrastructure that has not kept pace with headcount.
